title: Platform systems and services central playbook (Q4 2026)
author: Maya Singh
content:
Overview

This document is the centralized platform engineering playbook for Platform Systems & Services. It consolidates system inventory, how-tos, dashboards and alerting conventions, runbooks, recent retrospective findings, and the roadmap for Q4 2026. The goal is to provide an opinionated single source of truth for oncall, engineering, and product stakeholders.

Scope and audience

- Scope: Redwood Inference platform systems (control plane, ingress, routing, batching, cache, metrics pipeline, autoscaling, registry services) and supporting infra (Kubernetes clusters, GPU node pools, data plane APIs).
- Audience: Platform engineers, SREs, service owners, support engineers, and solutions engineers.

Systems & services inventory (high level)

1. control-plane-api (service)
   - Purpose: manage model metadata, rollout policies, feature flags, and routing decisions.
   - Owner: platform-control-plane
   - SLOs: p99 latency < 450ms, availability 99.95%

2. inference-router (service)
   - Purpose: route incoming inference requests to hosted/dedicated/private backends with policy evaluation (latency/cost/region).
   - Owner: runtime-routing
   - SLOs: p95 latency < 150ms, error rate < 0.05%

3. batching-worker (service)
   - Purpose: continuous batching and KV cache orchestration for GPU pools.
   - Owner: runtime-serving
   - SLOs: effective batching increases throughput by >= 2x for 50% of workload, queue latency < 30ms

4. metrics-pipeline (infrastructure)
   - Purpose: ingest traces/metrics/logs, compute derived metrics, export to Grafana/Datadog.
   - Owner: observability
   - SLOs: metrics freshness < 60s for critical dashboards

How-tos (common tasks)

- Add a new dashboard (Grafana):
  1. Create a dashboard in the platform-org Grafana folder with the tag "platform".
  2. Use templated variables: cluster, pool, model_version, route.
  3. Add an annotations panel for deploys (CI tag) and incidents.
  4. Add dashboard id to the service README and this playbook.

- Deploy a minor runtime change (canary -> rollout):
  1. Create a canary revision and pin 5% traffic for 30 minutes.
  2. Monitor p95 latency, error rate, and cost-per-token for the canary.
  3. If metrics are stable, increase to 25% for 1 hour, then 100%.
  4. If regressions observed, rollback to previous stable revision and open a regression triage ticket.

- Onboarding a new customer to Dedicated:
  1. Confirm VPC peering and routing rules with network team.
  2. Provision dedicated GPU pools (minimum 4x A100 equivalent).
  3. Apply KMS integration for key management.
  4. Run acceptance suite: perf (p95 latency target), throughput (tokens/sec), reliability (failover between zones).

Dashboards & alerts

Principles:
- Dashboards are the source of truth for runbooks: every runbook references 1-3 primary dashboards.
- Alerts must be actionable, have a clear owner, and include a runbook link. Use severity tiers: P0 (pager), P1 (email + Slack), P2 (Slack only).

Primary dashboards (examples)
- Platform Overview (grafana id: 2121) - high level KPIs: total tokens, cost-per-token, platform error rate, active customers.
- Inference Router (grafana id: 2210) - routing latencies, fallback rate, region imbalance.
- Serving Pool Health (grafana id: 2244) - GPU utilization, queue depth, batch size distribution.
- Metrics Pipeline (grafana id: 2300) - ingestion lag, export errors, cardinality growth.

Alerting standards (summary table)

Alert name | Trigger | Severity | Owner | Runbook
control-plane-api-high-error-rate | > 0.5% errors over 5m or 1% over 1m | P0 | platform-control-plane | /runbooks/control-plane-api-high-error-rate
inference-router-p95-latency | p95 > 300ms for 5m | P0 | runtime-routing | /runbooks/inference-router-slow-path
metrics-pipeline-lag | > 120s ingestion lag | P1 | observability | /runbooks/metrics-pipeline-lag
serving-pool-gpu-saturation | GPU util > 92% for 10m | P1 | runtime-serving | /runbooks/serving-pool-scale
batching-queue-backlog | queue length > 500 requests for 5m | P1 | runtime-serving | /runbooks/batching-backlog

Alert lifecycle

1. Alert fires -> automated diagnostic run (k8s pod status, recent deploys, scaling events).
2. Pager/PD incident created for P0. Assign owner.
3. Follow the runbook steps. If mitigated, annotate incident with root cause hypothesis.
4. Post-incident, tag the alert with remediation (threshold change, dashboard tweak, playbook update).

Runbooks (extracted examples)

Runbook: inference-router-slow-path
Purpose: handle p95 latency regressions on inference routing.
Steps:
1. Check Grafana Inference Router dashboard (id: 2210). Note p95 and pod count.
2. Confirm recent deploys (CI annotations) in the last 30 minutes. If deploy, rollback.
3. Check k8s pod restarts and OOMs: kubectl -n platform get pods -l app=inference-router -o wide.
4. Confirm backend capacity: k8s autoscaler, GPU pool saturation, and model variant fallbacks.
5. If CPU saturation on router pods, scale deployment by +30% and notify infra-scaling.
6. If backend GPU saturation, trigger emergency scale (add nodes) or redirect low-priority customers to cheaper model variant.
7. Update incident ticket with offset, mitigation steps and close when p95 returns to baseline for 15m.

Retrospective (recent Q3 2026 highlights)

Summary: Q3 incidents were dominated by two trends: degraded metrics freshness after a metrics pipeline release and unexpected GPU saturation for a new customer workload.

Root causes identified:
- Metrics pipeline release increased cardinality on a critical metric, causing ingestion throughput collapse.
- New customer workload had atypical long-context sequences causing higher KV cache pressure and larger-than-expected batch sizes.

Actions taken:
- Reverted metrics release, implemented automated cardinality tests in CI for metrics-pipeline.
- Added dynamic cache-eviction heuristics and autoscaling rules for long-context workloads.
- Introduced a pre-onboarding perf test that simulates 75th/95th percentile sequence lengths.

Metrics of improvement:
- Metrics pipeline ingestion lag 95p dropped from 220s to 42s.
- GPU saturation P1 incidents reduced 70% month-over-month.

Roadmap (Q4 2026)

- Ownership and governance:
  - Complete service-level owners for remaining 8 services by 2026-11-30.
  - Publish oncall rota and escalation matrix in team wiki.

- Observability improvements:
  - Implement histogram percentiles for batch-size and queue-depth metrics (target: 2026-11-15).
  - Add automatic annotations for autoscaler events to Grafana.

- Runtime and cost optimizations:
  - Deploy quantization-aware routing experiments to reduce cost-per-token by 12% (A/B tests).
  - Expand intelligent batching heuristics to reduce tail latency for long-context traffic.

- Runbook and process work:
  - Add automated triage scripts for top 5 P0 alerts.
  - Run quarterly game-day focused on cross-team capacity planning (next: 2026-12-10).

Team wiki and ownership

- Oncall contacts:
  - Primary pager: platform-sre@redwood.com (rotation: team-sre-primary).
  - Backup pager: runtime-oncall@redwood.com (rotation: runtime-oncall).
  - PagerDuty services: PD service ids are listed in the Team Wiki (see related pages).

- Documentation locations:
  - Service READMEs: github.com/redwood/platform-services (internal).
  - Dashboards: Grafana (org: platform-org).
  - Runbooks: confluence /runbooks/ under eng-platform.

Appendix: operational checklist (quick)

- If P0: acknowledge in 2 minutes, assign owner, start incident document, follow runbook.
- For degradations not P0: create ticket, tag owner, perform mitigations, track in weekly triage.
- Post-incident: complete RCA within 5 business days, schedule follow-up for remediation.
